newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA'S MAHATHIR SAYS HAPPY RINGGIT LEVEL.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA'S MAHATHIR SAYS HAPPY RINGGIT LEVEL.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Friday he was happy with the level of ringgit against the U.S. dollar, despite the local unit's sharp recent falls.
"We are happy with the current level of the ringgit," he told reporters after a meeting of his ruling United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) party
"The value (of ringgit) went down, but for us it does not matter. But, we believe it will recover," he said, speaking in his native Bahasa Melayu language.

"When we defend (the ringgit), we find they (speculators) profit from our act. And we don't want them to profit," he said when asked if the government would intervene in the market to defend the ringgit.
"We find the fall of the ringgit (against the dollar) is not much if compared with the Deutschemark which has fallen by 17 percent. Our's only fell by five percent," he said.

He reiterated that he was opposed to speculators attacking currrencies. "As a matter of principle, I am still opposed to the fact that someone can fiddle around with our currency ... our sovereignty," Mahathir said.
"For as long as people like Soros can fiddle around with the currencies of other countries, their sovereignty will never be safe," he said.
Mahathir has said that U.S. fund manager George Soros was responsible for the recent speculative attack on all Southeast Asian currencies.
The ringgit has been under heavy selling pressure for over a month. It has declined from around 2.50 a dollar a month ago to 2.66 after Mahathir's remarks on Friday.
After abandoning an initial defense in the open market, Malaysia allowed the currency to depreciate.
But last Sunday, the central bank imposed a capital flow restriction by ordering local banks to limit their currency swaps transactions to $2.0 million per overseas customer.
